description: We’re Binary Coders, a team passionate about coding, space exploration, and creative problem-solving. We’re building Lunar Base: Mission Trainer, an interactive game where players manage a lunar base and tackle challenges on the Moon. We’re looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled or interested in web development, UI/UX design, game design, space science, and research. Beginners are welcome!
summary: Junior Astronauts Mission Trainer (Lunar Academy) is a zero-login, browser-playable lunar habitat survival simulator grounded in real NASA data. Built for students and aspiring explorers, it turns closed-loop astronautics into an interactive 3 pillar challenge balancing Life Support, Power & Thermal, and Radiation Shielding where every decision carries a real physical trade-off and live space-weather consequences.
details:
What it does & how it works:

Junior Astronauts Mission Trainer (Lunar Academy) is an instant-play, browser-based lunar habitat survival simulator grounded in real NASA data. Operating on a discrete time-step loop, the telemetry dashboard unifies habitat operations into three core resource pillars governed by engineering trade-offs:

1. Life Support (Air & Water Loop): Regulates cabin oxygen, carbon dioxide scrubbing, and water recycling. Trade-off: Keeping cabin air safe and clean consumes battery reserves and potable water tanks.

2. Power & Thermal Balance (Energy & Greenhouse): Balances solar arrays, battery storage, greenhouse grow lights, heaters, and thermal louvers across extreme lunar day and night cycles. Trade-off: Sealing louvers and running heaters to stay warm during freezing lunar nights drains power quickly.

3. Shielding & Radiation (Protection & PSR Rover): Uses habitat water tanks as radiation shielding against cosmic rays and solar storms, while deploying dust shields and sending rovers to mine water ice in shadowed craters. Trade-off: Using water for oxygen production reduces radiation protection; gathering ice water exposes the rover and crew to higher radiation and oxygen burn.


What benefits does it have & intended impact:

- Zero-Friction Accessibility: Requires no downloads, installations, or user accounts—students, teachers, and judges can launch a guest mission in any web browser within seconds.

- Real-World Cause-and-Effect Learning: When critical thresholds are crossed (such as high carbon dioxide, low oxygen, solar storms, or lunar nightfall), contextual pop-up diagnostics explain the physiological impact on crew vitals (Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, oxygen levels, Hydration) and offer one-click trade-off decisions.

- Non-Punitive Replayability: Randomized mission scenarios and a post-mission Black-Box Root-Cause Debrief help learners understand why a failure happened and immediately test a better strategy.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used:

- Languages: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3.

- Frontend Software & Hosting: Next.js (React), custom pure-CSS space atmosphere styling, and icons, deployed on Vercel.

- Backend & Database: Node.js, Express.js, and MongoDB Atlas, deployed on Render with a pre-flight boot sequence for smooth initialization.

- NASA Data & Datasets: Integrated with the NASA Space Weather database for solar flare alerts, alongside curated baselines from NASA human spaceflight standards, life-support mass-balance records, lunar thermal profiles, and plant habitat trials.

- Development Tools: Standard laptops for testing, Git and GitHub for version control, and presentation software for pitch decks.


How is your project creative & what factors did your team consider?

- Water-as-Shielding & Greenhouse Coupling: Instead of treating resources as isolated bars, our system links subsystems creatively using water tanks simultaneously as radiation shielding and insulation during freezing lunar nights.

- Rapid CSS Spacecraft HUD Without Heavy 3D Assets: By crafting a high-contrast mission-control interface purely with CSS styling and tabular telemetry instead of heavy 3D downloads, the simulator loads fast on low-bandwidth connections.

- Avoiding Cognitive Overload & Eliminating "Free" Choices: Young learners can become overwhelmed by too many gauges, so we distilled complex space math into three clear pillars guided by educational pop-ups, ensuring every button carries a real power, water, or radiation cost.
